Markov-Order Adequacy Test

Source: R/markov_order_test_htna.R
markov_order_test_htna.Rd

htna-named wrapper for Nestimate::markov_order_test(). Tests whether a first-order Markov model is adequate for the observed sequences, or whether a higher order is required, by comparing the empirical transition structure against orders 1..max_order via permutation.

Usage

markov_order_test_htna(data, ...)

Arguments

data

An htna network from build_htna(), or raw sequence data: a list of character vectors or a wide-format data frame. See Nestimate::markov_order_test().

...

Additional arguments passed to Nestimate::markov_order_test(), such as max_order, n_perm, alpha, parallel, n_cores, and seed. See that function for the full, current argument list.

Value

An object of class net_markov_order with components optimal_order (sequential permutation-test order), bic_order, aic_order, test_table (a data frame with one row per tested order and columns order, loglik, AIC, BIC, df, g2, p_permutation, p_asymptotic, significant), the permutation null distributions, fitted transition matrices, and the inputs. print(), summary() and plot() methods are supplied by Nestimate; see Nestimate::markov_order_test().

Details

Accepts an htna network directly (its session sequences are tested), or raw sequence data (a list of character vectors or a wide-format data frame). Use alongside reliability_htna() and casedrop_reliability_htna() when assessing whether a Markov-1 transition network is appropriate before trusting downstream htna analyses.

The orders are tested sequentially: optimal_order is the highest order k for which every step from order j - 1 to j, j = 1, ..., k, is significant at alpha. It is therefore one less than the first order whose step is not significant, and equals max_order when every step is significant (in which case the search should be widened). The BIC- and AIC-preferred orders are reported alongside.

Suffixed _htna to avoid clashing with Nestimate::markov_order_test() when both packages are loaded.

See also

reliability_htna(), casedrop_reliability_htna(), centrality_stability_htna().

Examples

data(human_ai)
net <- build_htna(human_ai, actor_type = "actor_type")
#> A network with one long sequence is not recommended and can't be validated using bootstrap and other confirmatory testings.
#> Metadata aggregated per session: ties resolved by first occurrence in 'session_date' (1 sessions), 'cluster' (42 sessions), 'actor_type' (24 sessions)
# Few permutations to keep the example fast; use the default 500 in practice.
markov_order_test_htna(net, max_order = 2, n_perm = 20, seed = 1)
#> Markov Order Test  [within-w permutation, n_perm = 20, alpha = 0.050]
#>   428 sequences / 19346 observations / 12 states
#> 
#>   Selected order  BIC: 1   AIC: 2   permutation-LRT: 2
#> 
#>  order    loglik      AIC      BIC   df       g2 p_permutation p_asymptotic
#>      0 -43741.91 87505.83 87592.40   NA       NA            NA           NA
#>      1 -37315.96 74899.92 75954.53  121 12815.99    0.04761905            0
#>      2 -33812.56 70683.12 82716.72 1272  6481.76    0.04761905            0
#>  significant
#>           NA
#>         TRUE
#>         TRUE
